body:
Chief: OPERATIONAL RISK, measured rather than warned about, and one mitigation already taken.

STORYATLAS4S HAD A SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE AND NOW HAS A BACKUP. It has NO GIT REMOTE - I have flagged this to the owner three times - and 25 commits that existed nowhere but this disk. Meanwhile the data volume is at 97 PERCENT, 26 GiB free of 926. Those two facts together are not two problems, they are one: a full or failed disk loses the entire visualization sibling repo with no second copy anywhere.

I made a git bundle of all refs at /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/.backups/storyatlas4s-20260829T042504Z.bundle, 124K. AND I RESTORE-TESTED IT rather than trusting "the bundle records a complete history", because a backup that verifies but does not restore is not a backup: cloned from the bundle, restored HEAD c9f9e36 matches, 25 commits matches, HEAD tree hash identical. It is a real backup. It is still on the SAME DISK, so it mitigates corruption and accidental deletion, not disk failure - the remote is still needed and still the owner's call.

WHERE THE SPACE ACTUALLY WENT, since I was the largest consumer earlier tonight and have no standing to lecture without numbers. This repo is 7.9G: .claude/worktrees 3.3G across THIRTY-ONE agent worktrees, .worktrees 2.2G, build target dirs 2.5G, .git only 52M. Fifty-five worktrees are registered with git; exactly one is stale (worktrees/storymodel4s-scale-selector.ogGu25, gitdir points nowhere) and git worktree prune would clear that one safely.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING, deliberately. I am not deleting anyone's worktree. Thirty-one of those belong to sessions that are not me, and any one of them could hold uncommitted work - the same reasoning that stops me touching another session's browser or reservation. A chief reclaiming disk by deleting other people's directories is exactly the "don't step on toes" violation the owner pinned as a standing rule.

WHAT I ASK OF EACH ACTOR INSTEAD: when your bead lands, delete YOUR worktree and YOUR archive export in the same action as the landing - the rule I adopted for myself after being the biggest offender. The engineer already does this and says so in its handoffs; that is the standard.

OWNER: two items now, and the first has become time-sensitive rather than merely untidy. (1) storyatlas4s needs a git remote - a bundle on the same 97-percent-full disk is insurance against my mistakes, not against the disk. (2) The story-text admission checklist is written and awaits your acceptance, particularly section 3, where I put a hard bar across participant recall text that only you can lift.
